claude.sample_unit: notes and LLM outputs analyzed for error codification

links.outcome: Generalizability across institutions of adapted prompts versus zero-shot prompts for smoking history extraction
links.effect: Adapted prompts, engineered to address observed errors, achieved better generalizability across institutions than zero-shot prompts; macro-F1 0.86 in VA, 0.85 in MIMIC.
links.quote: We demonstrate that adapted prompts, engineered to address observed errors, achieve better generalizability across institutions compared to zero-shot prompts.

links.outcome: Error hazard distributions between development-like (MIMIC) and VA institutional datasets
links.effect: Overall accuracy was similar (macro-F1 0.86 VA, 0.85 MIMIC), but hazard distributions varied significantly; templated information more prevalent in VA notes (p adj=0.004).
links.quote: While overall accuracy with the adapted prompt was similar between institutions (macro-F1=0.86 in VA, 0.85 in MIMIC), hazard distributions varied significantly.

unlisted_practices: Hazard-framework error codification to distinguish generalization failures from inherent data differences

links.effect: Errors in the untrained institution were more frequent despite similar hazard prevalence (p adj =0.007).
links.quote: However, when task-specific requirements conflicted with pre-trained model behavior, errors in the untrained institution were more frequent despite similar hazard prevalence (p adj =0.007), showing a limit of LLM generalizability.

links.effect: Adapted LLM identified eligibility in 59% versus 8% with current national VA tools.
links.quote: As a potential clinical application, our adapted LLM system identified lung cancer screening eligibility in 59% of Veterans who later developed the disease, compared to 8% with current national VA tools.

links.effect: Adapted prompt macro-F1=0.86 in VA and 0.85 in MIMIC; hazard distributions varied significantly.
links.quote: While overall accuracy with the adapted prompt was similar between institutions (macro-F1=0.86 in VA, 0.85 in MIMIC), hazard distributions varied significantly.
